# Taxonomy of Grid-Based Logic Games

## Primary Categories by Core Mechanic

---

### 1. LOOP-DRAWING PUZZLES
*Objective: Draw a single continuous, non-crossing loop*

#### 1.1 Unconstrained Path
- **Slitherlink** — Loop drawn between dots; numbers indicate how many sides of a cell are used
- **Masyu** — Loop must pass through all circles; black/white circles impose turn/straight rules

#### 1.2 Directionally Constrained
- **Nagareru** — Wind direction restricts loop movement; arrows define directional flow
- **Suraromu** — Loop must pass through all "Gates" in a numbered sequence
- **Moon-or-Sun** — Loop passes through rooms once; must alternate between moon and sun cells

#### 1.3 Cell-Condition Constrained
- **Dotchi-Loop** — Loop passes through white circles; per bold-line area, all circles are either all straight or all turning
- **Mid-loop** — Black circles must be the midpoint of a straight line segment of the loop
- **Yajilin** — Loop avoids black cells and numbered cells; arrow-numbers indicate black cell counts in a direction

---

### 2. CELL-SHADING / PAINTING PUZZLES
*Objective: Determine which cells to color black (or shade)*

#### 2.1 Shape-Constrained Shading
- **Choco Banana** — Black cells must form rectangles/squares; white cells must not form rectangles/squares
- **Shakashaka** — Place triangles in cells so remaining white areas always form rectangles/squares
- **Sto-stone** — Shade cells per room counts; when "dropped" downward, shaded cells fill the bottom half exactly

#### 2.2 Connectivity-Constrained Shading
- **Nurikabe** — White cell islands defined by numbers; black cells form one connected wall with no 2×2 blocks
- **Kurodoko** — Numbers indicate total visible white cells in cross directions; black cells cannot touch
- **Heyawake** — Rooms have black cell counts; black cells cannot touch; white cells cannot span more than two rooms
- **Hitori** — Shade cells so no number repeats in any row/column; black cells cannot touch; white cells stay connected

#### 2.3 Neighbor-Count Shading
- **Kurotto** — Circles show sum of connected black cells extending from them
- **Usowan** — Numbers show adjacent black cell count, but exactly one number per bold-line region is deliberately wrong
- **Akari** — Place light bulbs in white cells; numbered cells indicate adjacent bulbs; all white cells must be illuminated

#### 2.4 Pattern/Tetromino Shading
- **LITS** — Shade one tetromino per bold-line region; same-shaped tetrominoes cannot touch; shaded cells connected; no 2×2
- **Norinori** — Place dominoes (pairs of black cells) so each bold-line region contains exactly two black cells
- **Tilepaint** — Color entire "tiles" (bold-line regions); diagonal-number cells constrain black cell counts in rows/columns; solution depicts an object
- **Nurimeizu** — Paint rooms entirely or leave white; creates a maze from S to G; circles on shortest path, triangles not on it

---

### 3. NUMBER-PLACEMENT PUZZLES
*Objective: Fill cells with numbers according to constraints*

#### 3.1 Latin Square / Uniqueness
- **Sudoku** — Place 1–9 in each row, column, and 3×3 box
- **Hitori** — Eliminate duplicates in rows/columns by shading (see also §2.2)

#### 3.2 Region-Based Number Fill
- **Fillomino** — Fill grid with numbers; each number defines a block of that many connected cells; same-size blocks cannot touch
- **Ripple Effect** — Each bold-line room contains 1 to N; duplicate numbers in a row/column must be separated by at least that number of cells
- **Makaro** — Each room contains 1 to N; arrow-cells indicate which neighbor holds the largest value; same numbers in adjacent rooms cannot touch

#### 3.3 Crossword-Style Number Placement
- **Nansuke** — Fill blank cells with digits from a given list; numbers read horizontally or vertically

---

### 4. REGION-DIVISION PUZZLES
*Objective: Partition the grid into regions satisfying shape or size rules*

#### 4.1 Rectangular Regions
- **Shikaku** — Divide grid into rectangles; each rectangle contains exactly one number equal to its cell count

#### 4.2 Fixed-Size Polyomino Regions
- **Five Cells** — Divide grid into pentominoes (exactly 5 cells each); numbers indicate how many block-boundary lines surround a cell

#### 4.3 Shape-Matched Regions
- **Double Choco** — Divide into blocks each containing a white and a gray area of identical shape (rotation/mirror allowed)
- **Sashigane** — Divide into L-shaped blocks; circles mark the bend; arrows point toward the bend from an end

#### 4.4 Evolving / Sequential Shape Regions
- **Evolomino** — Blocks grow by one cell along an arrow path; each successive block adds one square without rotation or flipping

---

### 5. PATH / MOVEMENT PUZZLES
*Objective: Move or connect elements across the grid*

#### 5.1 Circle/Token Movement
- **Satogaeri** — Move circles into their home country; numbers indicate distance traveled; paths cannot cross
- **Yosenabe** — Move numbered circles into gray areas; gray area numbers must match sum of entering circles; arrows cannot cross

#### 5.2 Connection / Bridge Building
- **Hashiwokakero** — Connect numbered islands with bridges; bridge count matches island number; all islands connected; max two bridges between any pair
- **Numberlink** — Connect matching number pairs with non-crossing, non-overlapping paths that fill the grid

#### 5.3 Sequential Snake Placement
- **Hebi** — Place snakes (sequences 1–5) in white cells; snakes cannot touch; directional vision rules restrict placement relative to other snakes

---

### 6. MARKING / SYMBOL-PLACEMENT PUZZLES
*Objective: Place specific symbols or marks in cells*

#### 6.1 Directional Marks
- **Juosan** — Fill every cell with — or |; territory numbers indicate the difference in count; marks cannot extend more than two cells in the perpendicular direction

#### 6.2 Geometric Marks
- **Shakashaka** — Place corner triangles so white remainders are always rectangular *(see also §2.1)*

#### 6.3 Square/Block Marks
- **Evolomino** — Place squares in cells forming growing blocks along arrow paths *(see also §4.4)*

---

### 7. HYBRID / MULTI-CONSTRAINT PUZZLES
*Puzzles combining shading, numbering, and region logic*

- **Chained Block** — Black cell blocks must form chains (corner-touching); each block labeled with size or "?"; no two same-shaped blocks in one chain
- **Nuritwin** — Each region contains exactly two same-size shaded blocks; all shaded cells globally connected; blocks in same region cannot touch
- **Nurimisaki** — Circles are "promontory" cells with exactly one white neighbor; numbers indicate white cell line length; no 2×2 white or black
- **Pencils** — Identify pencil shapes (straight runs) and draw lines from their tips; line length matches number in pencil
- **Tilepaint** — Whole tiles colored or not; diagonal clue cells constrain counts *(see also §2.4)*

---

## Cross-Cutting Structural Dimensions

| Dimension | Examples |
|---|---|
| **Single loop output** | Slitherlink, Masyu, Dotchi-Loop, Nagareru, Moon-or-Sun, Mid-loop, Suraromu, Yajilin |
| **Uses bold-line regions/rooms** | Heyawake, Ripple Effect, Makaro, LITS, Norinori, Moon-or-Sun, Nurimeizu, Nuritwin, Sto-stone, Suraromu, Tilepaint, Usowan |
| **Connectivity of shaded cells required** | Nurikabe, LITS, Nuritwin |
| **Connectivity of white cells required** | Hitori, Kurodoko, Heyawake, Nurimisaki, Nurimeizu |
| **No 2×2 same-color blocks** | Nurikabe, Nurimisaki, Nuritwin, Nurimeizu |
| **Arrow/directional clues** | Yajilin, Makaro, Sashigane, Evolomino, Hebi, Yosenabe, Juosan |
| **Number = region/block size** | Fillomino, Shikaku, Five Cells, Nurikabe, Ripple Effect |
